summary.en: Hezbollah explosives seized in two Lebanese trucks have prompted Lebanon's prime minister and security forces to promise a thorough investigation, while Israeli artillery and air strikes continue against Hezbollah positions in southern Lebanon, causing civilian casualties. In northern Israel, a Hezbollah submunition exploded in a teenager's backpack during a hike near the Lebanon border, killing Elazar Yair Wilensky and wounding dozens, leading the IDF chief to order a probe and authorities to consider restricting hikes. Students on the same hike fashioned tourniquets from belts and socks after the blast. Hezbollah announced compensation for Lebanese homeowners whose houses were destroyed and unveiled an aid plan for displaced civilians. The UCDP recorded 4,335 battle-related deaths in 2024.
summary.nb: Hezbollah-eksplosiver som ble beslaglagt i to libanesiske lastebiler har fått Libanons statsminister og sikkerhetsstyrker til å love en grundig etterforskning, mens israelsk artilleri og luftangrep fortsetter mot Hezbollah-posisjoner i sørlige Libanon, og forårsaker sivile tap. I Nord-Israel eksploderte en Hezbollah-submunisjon i en tenårings ryggsekk under en fottur nær Libanongränsen, og drepte Elazar Yair Wilensky og såret dusinvis, noe som fikk IDF-sjefen til å beordre en undersøkelse og myndighetene til å vurdere restriksjoner på fotturer. Studenter på samme tur laget tourniquetter av belter og sokker etter eksplosjonen. Hezbollah kunngjorde erstatning til libanesiske huseiere hvis hus ble ødelagt og presenterte en hjelpsplan for fortrengte sivile. UCDP registrerte 4 335 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024.

background.title: Hezbollah–Israel conflict (2023–present)
background.extract: An ongoing conflict between the Lebanese militant group Hezbollah and Israel began on 8 October 2023, when Hezbollah launched rockets and artillery at Israeli positions following Hamas's October 7 attacks on Israel. The conflict escalated into a prolonged exchange of bombardments, leading to extensive displacement in Israel and Lebanon. The conflict is part of the broader Middle Eastern crisis that began with Hamas's attack, with the short Israeli invasion of Lebanon in 2024 marking the largest escalation of the Hezbollah–Israel conflict since the 2006 Lebanon War. In Arabic, the conflict (2023–2024) is referred to as the "Support War" or the "Gaza Support War."
